\section{Stage 9: the edit window}\label{app:stage9}

\providecommand{\SnineCI}[3]{#1\,{\scriptsize[#2, #3]}}% an estimate and its 95 % interval, inline
\providecommand{\SnineSt}[3]{\begin{tabular}[t]{@{}c@{}}#1\\[-1.5pt]{\tiny[#2, #3]}\end{tabular}}% the same, stacked

Stage 9 tested when the writing token can still change the answer: from what depth a patch of its cached key and value still moves the answer, with and without the candidates listed after the context. This appendix gives the design, the frozen prediction note, the runs, every verdict (\cref{tab:stage9}) with the per-model results, what did not hold and what is post hoc; the main-text account is in \cref{sec:claim3}.

\subsection{Design}\label{app:s9-design}

\paragraph{Models and populations.} Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \citep{jiang2023mistral,grattafiori2024llama3,yang2024qwen25}, at the revisions of \cref{tab:models-j}, with $L$ = \NqLayersMistralSeven{}, \NqLayersLlamaEight{} and \NqLayersQwenSeven{} blocks; BF16, sdpa attention, one A100-SXM4-80GB. N9: \NqStories{} new story cores, drawn with a new seed from a stream that excludes every core tuple drawn by any earlier stage, rendered like part B's fresh stories (\cref{app:prompts-fresh}); clusters (lexicon, base, source). C: part B's \NqCalib{} calibration cores, used there only to discover answer frames; here they only fix $l_b$. E9: \NqCores{} new cores in the original lexicon, disjoint from every earlier population and meeting part C's pair-swap condition (\cref{app:prompts-intervention}); clusters (base, source). Passages: part A's \NqPassages{} evaluation items (set E; \cref{app:prompts-natural}) decide; its \NqPassagesR{} frame items (set R), never patched before, are a held-out check that decides nothing; clusters: articles.

\paragraph{Formats.} Stories: \fmtNone{} (NONE), \fmtBefore{} (BEFORE), \fmtNull{} (POST-NULL), \fmtPost{} (POST), \fmtListA{} (AFTER) and \fmtLetter{} (LETTER), as in part B; the edits use NONE, AFTER, LETTER and POST, which share the prefix up to the writing token. Passages: free form (NOM), options before (OPTB) and options after (OPTA); lettered options (LETA) were exploratory. BEFORE and OPTB keep the answer space of AFTER and OPTA with the list before the context; POST-NULL matches POST's length without naming a candidate.

\paragraph{Patches and the two depths.} Each row runs the base prompt B and sets the writing token's cached key and value (passages: over the answer span) in every block, to those of the source run S inside the row's window and to B's own outside it. The \emph{late} patch with onset $l$ writes S in blocks $l$ to $L-1$, the \emph{early} patch in blocks 0 to $l-1$; together they equal the full patch KV@0, which is the S run (tested in FP32). Onsets are every second block for stories and $\mathrm{round}(xL)$, $x \in \{0.15, 0.3, 0.45, 0.6\}$, for passages; key-only and value-only rows are reported. $l_c(f)$ is the first onset whose late patch moves fewer than half of the competent answers in format $f$ to S ($L$ if none), recomputed in every bootstrap resample. $l_b$ is the first onset whose late patch moves at most 0.2 of the AFTER answers of the C cores; it was written to a file before any N9 item was scored and re-derived by the scorer: $l_b$ = \NqLbMistralSeven{}, \NqLbLlamaEight{} and \NqLbQwenSeven{} ($l_b/L$ = \NqLbFracMistralSeven{}, \NqLbFracLlamaEight{} and \NqLbFracQwenSeven{}).

\paragraph{Edits.} At blocks 3, 7, 11 and 15 an edit writes a target $t \in \{\mathrm{S}, \mathrm{X}\}$ into the writing token's residual stream, which reaches later tokens only through the token's keys and values (\cref{app:law}), so it is applied as a cache row: nat ($t$'s own states); E1, part C's single-site steering vector (\cref{app:edits}); E4b, part C's rank-16 remap trained at the writing token, as stored (no basis exists for Llama); and CAA, E1's vector added at every position from the writing token on, generated tokens included, as in contrastive activation addition \citep{panickssery2023caa}. Dose rows at blocks 3 and 7 move both cached states, or one, a fraction $\alpha$ of the way from B's to $t$'s, and scale E1. The key share $r_K = \langle \Delta K_Z, \Delta K_t\rangle / \langle \Delta K_t, \Delta K_t\rangle$, with $\Delta K$ the displacement of the writing token's keys from B's (all heads, blocks $l{+}1$ on), is the fraction of the natural key displacement an edit $Z$ delivers ($\alpha$ for the interpolations; CAA's equals E1's).

\paragraph{Answers and statistics.} Answers are generated greedily: in stories and edits up to 16 tokens, stopped at the first candidate (LETTER: the first letter); in passages up to 48 tokens, scored by whole-word containment after a normalisation applied to every candidate alike. Each format uses its competent items, whose identity row answers B and whose clean S run answers S. A row's \emph{flip} is its share of answers equal to S (edits: to $t$); among the answers that are not S, the share equal to B and the median absolute $p(\mathrm{B})$ of those B answers (trie scorer of part B) measure a silent failure. Intervals are 95\,\% two-stage cluster-bootstrap intervals (10{,}000 resamples, seed 20261015), with one index set per population shared by all rows, so contrasts are paired. A model's verdict levels are defined below \cref{tab:stage9}; a line is supported if supported in all three models, at the point if at least at the point in all three, and not supported if any model is not (P2p: two of three at the point). Falsifiers are read at the point; there is no multiplicity correction.

The note (dated 2026-10-14) fixes the predictions, thresholds, falsifiers, primary analysis and a reading for each outcome; a specification written the same day fixes everything the code computes. Both were committed in the first freeze commit (2026-10-15), before any stage-9 GPU session, and the GPU script refused to run if either file or the code differed from the latest freeze. Neither file changed at the refreeze (\cref{app:s9-runs}); every session's guard recorded their sha256:\\[2pt]
{\small\begin{tabular}{@{}ll@{}}
note & \texttt{3e97d03198de057cc50ec6f9147487c19125d7cfbb05e601ee79cd4151a8f056}\\
specification & \texttt{ca9efe813d81deb8102baa8cf2751474e1f22e96457e11cd77419d08867315b0}
\end{tabular}}\\[2pt]
It is a dated note, not a preregistration entry: unlike entries A--J it records no class or prior per line and no Holm family. The pattern it tests was found in stages 1--8 (post hoc); what it decides on was unseen: the new cores, the early windows, the window rows on passages, generated answers under a window, the dose rows and all-position steering.

\Cref{tab:stage9} gives each prediction and falsifier in the note's wording, shortened. It omits two conditions: P5b is evaluable only if the natural patch's $\tau$ at block 3 is at least 0.9 (it is \NqTauNatThreeMistralSeven{} and \NqTauNatThreeQwenSeven{}), and B3's units are (core, target, edit) for the E1 multiples, E4b and the joint interpolations, in the blocks where the natural patch transfers (\fmtListA{} flip $\geq 0.9$: block 3, and block 7 at Qwen) and among units whose \fmtNone{} answer is the target. In the note, F2 would mean that the multiple-choice answer space, not the list's position, closes the window (an evaluation warning), and B-F2 that the value curve is as convex as the key curve; $\psi_C(f, \alpha)$ is the identity effect of a channel-$C$ interpolation as a share of the natural channel-$C$ patch's (double difference over the targets S and X of the trie score, in nats).

\paragraph{Pre-written readings.} The outcome selects three. F2 triggers: ``report only the evaluation warning (`intervention verdicts depend on the answer format'), in the appendix, with no mechanism claim.'' P5c transfers: ``state the claim for single-site edits, patching and KV-cache edits only.'' B1 and B2 fail: ``describe the convexity without a threshold claim. The failed channel-ratio law stays reported as failed.'' The two readings written for the window are not used. The first requires P1--P3 on stories at least at the point and F1--F3 not triggered, but P3s fails at Mistral and F2 triggers. The second (``Late edits fail silently with listed candidates; the early window also moves free-form answers, so the routes overlap in depth.'') requires P1 to hold, which it does not, and its second clause is false here (F1 is not triggered). The wording of the window in the main text is therefore post hoc. The note also requires depths per model, never a universal depth. % verbatim: docs/STAGE9_PREDICTIONS.md section 6; selection: docs/stage9/OUTCOME.md

\subsection{The runs}\label{app:s9-runs}

Session 0 (2026-10-21), at the first freeze, stopped at the FP32 test gate before any model was fetched or loaded (284 tests: 280 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed) and produced no stage-9 number; the failing test, from part C's code, reads the release of \citet{prakash2025lookbacks}, which the stage-9 script did not fetch and no stage-9 step uses. The refreeze (2026-10-21) carried only pipeline fixes: fetching that release before the gate; a guard check, prompted by a read-only audit of the run path, that refuses an output directory holding another freeze's record (which would have made every verdict not evaluable); a self-repairing release cache; and a float tolerance of $10^{-4}$ in a gate test that compares two processes' output, since FP32 CPU kernels are not bitwise reproducible across processes. The note, specification, populations, steps and scorer did not change; a CPU run of the whole pipeline from a fresh clone passed first. Session 1 (2026-10-21, deadline 6 hours) ran every step except the Mistral and Llama edits, cut at their deadline reserves after 42 and 28 of the \NqCores{} cores (54 and 34 minutes), and those models' exploratory LETA steps. Session 2 (2026-10-22, deadline 8 hours), at the same freeze commit and on the same results, as the design provides for steps cut by the deadline, reran those edits from the start (28 and 26 minutes) and ran the LETA steps; all 24 steps finished. (The run log numbers the sessions from 1.) The specification estimated about 25 minutes per model for the edits: at session 1's pace the Mistral and Llama steps would have needed about 100, four times the estimate, while session 2's reruns stayed near it, and Qwen's edit evaluation took 16 minutes of per-core time in session 1 (about 32 with its check step, as the outcome record gives it). % docs/stage9/RUN_LOG.md, OUTCOME.md; per-core minutes summed from results/gpu_stage9/logs/ed_*.log; Qwen's check step: logs/chk_ed_qwen7.log (17:50 to 18:08)

\paragraph{Checks and controls.} Both sessions passed the FP32 gate (in the last, \NqTestsPassed{} tests passed, \NqTestsSkipped{} were skipped and \NqTestsFailed{} failed in the \NqTestFiles{} stage-9 test files) and recorded the same freeze and hashes; every results file records the freeze commit and a clean tree, and a local re-score reproduces the score file exactly, paths aside. The $l_b$ re-derived from the C rows equals the file the evaluation read. T\_check, the largest difference between S's residual written as an edit and the natural tables, is \NqTcheckMistralSeven{}, \NqTcheckLlamaEight{} and \NqTcheckQwenSeven{}. In stories, the full patch moves \NqFullMin{}--\NqFullMax{} of all items; \NqCompetentMin{}--\NqCompetentMax{} of the stories are competent per format; the BF16 floor, the identity row against the clean B run of the same item in another batch shape, is \NqFloorMin{}--\NqFloorMax{} nats of mean absolute trie score and changes \NqFloorArgMin{}--\NqFloorArgMax{} of argmax answers, while two identity rows in one batch are bitwise equal; and the argmax of the trie score, a sensitivity analysis like strict matching and all-items versions, agrees with the generated answer in \NqEargGenMin{}--\NqEargGenMax{} of rows.

\subsection{Verdicts and per-model results}\label{app:s9-results}

Of the ten counted lines (P1--P4, P5a, P5b, POST and B1--B3), \NqTotSupported{} are supported, \NqTotAtPoint{} supported at the point, \NqTotNotSupported{} not supported and \NqTotNotEvaluable{} not evaluable; F2 triggers, on passages at Qwen (\cref{tab:stage9}).


\paragraph{Stories (\cref{tab:s9window}).} With the candidates listed after the story (\fmtListA{}, \fmtLetter{}) the late window closes at \NqLcFracListedMin{}--\NqLcFracListedMax{} of the depth, in \fmtListA{} \NqGapNoneAfterMin{}--\NqGapNoneAfterMax{}\,$L$ earlier than in \fmtNone{}, while with the same list before the story it closes \NqGapBeforeAfterMin{}--\NqGapBeforeAfterMax{}\,$L$ later than in \fmtListA{} (F2s not triggered); at $l_b$ the early patch moves \NqEarlyListedMin{}--\NqEarlyListedMax{} of the listed answers and \NqEarlyFreeMax{} of those in \fmtNone{}, \fmtBefore{} and \fmtNull{}. In \fmtListA{} at $l_b$, \NqSilentShareAfterMin{}--\NqSilentShareAfterMax{} of the answers the late patch does not move to S are the stale B, with median $p(\mathrm{B})$ \NqSilentPbAfterMistralSeven{} at Mistral (reported: \NqSilentPbAfterLlamaEight{} at Llama, \NqSilentPbAfterQwenSeven{} at Qwen), and the same patch moves the \fmtNone{} answer but not the \fmtListA{} answer in \NqInconsMin{}--\NqInconsMax{} of the stories (reported). The key alone moves \NqKzeroListedMin{}--\NqKzeroListedMax{} of the listed answers and \NqKzeroFreeMax{} of those in \fmtNone{} and \fmtBefore{}, the value alone \NqVzeroListedMin{}--\NqVzeroListedMax{} and \NqVzeroFreeMin{}--\NqVzeroFreeMax{}: the split of part B (reported).

\paragraph{Edits (\cref{tab:s9edits}).} E1 tracks the natural patch within 0.1 in \NqEoneWithinAll{} of the \NqEoneCellsAll{} format $\times$ block cells. E4b moves \NqEfourbNoneMin{}--\NqEfourbNoneMax{} of the free-form answers but transfers little to \fmtListA{} (transfer ratio $\tau = \text{flip}(\text{\fmtListA})/\text{flip}(\text{\fmtNone})$ = \NqTauEfourbThreeMistralSeven{} and \NqTauEfourbThreeQwenSeven{} at block 3, \NqTauEfourbBeyondMin{}--\NqTauEfourbBeyondMax{} beyond), with a key share of \NqEditRkEfourbThreeMistralSeven{} and \NqEditRkEfourbThreeQwenSeven{} at block 3, lower deeper (post hoc observation). Where the natural patch moves \NqPfivecNatReadMin{}--\NqPfivecNatReadMax{} of the \fmtListA{} answers, CAA moves \NqPfivecCaaMin{}--\NqPfivecCaaMax{} (P5c: transfers in all three models), so the window claim is made for single-site edits, patching and KV-cache edits only. P5c reads \fmtListA{} alone. With lettered options CAA moves only \NqEditCaaLetterFifteenQwenSeven{}--\NqEditCaaLetterFifteenMistralSeven{} of the answers in the same cells (natural patch \NqEditNatLetterFifteenMistralSeven{}--\NqEditNatLetterElevenMistralSeven{}), and at block 3 \NqEditCaaLetterThreeQwenSeven{}--\NqEditCaaLetterThreeMistralSeven{} against the natural patch's \NqEditNatLetterThreeQwenSeven{}--\NqEditNatLetterThreeLlamaEight{} (reported): with letters, steering at every position mostly does not escape the window (least so at Mistral), and inside it reaches fewer answers than the patch. CAA also moves fewer free-form answers than E1 at Qwen's blocks 3 and 7 (\NqEditCaaNoneThreeQwenSeven{}, \NqEditCaaNoneSevenQwenSeven{}; reported). CAA writes at every later position, the later mentions and the answer included, so it is not an edit of the stored value alone.

\paragraph{Dose and the key share (\cref{tab:s9dose}).} $r_K$ separates the edits that transfer to \fmtListA{} from those that do not with AUC \NqAucMin{}--\NqAucMax{} (B3 supported), and the fixed rule $r_K \geq 0.8$ predicts transfer with accuracy \NqRuleAccMin{}--\NqRuleAccMax{}; always predicting transfer would be right for \fpeval{round(\NqAucPosMistralSeven/\NqAucUnitsMistralSeven,2)}, \fpeval{round(\NqAucPosLlamaEight/\NqAucUnitsLlamaEight,2)} and \fpeval{round(\NqAucPosQwenSeven/\NqAucUnitsQwenSeven,2)} of the units (arithmetic on \cref{tab:s9dose}), so the rule beats that base rate only at Qwen (post hoc comparison). B3's units lie inside the window, where the natural patch transfers; beyond it a key share near the natural one does not help, since the natural patch ($r_K = 1$) itself fails there. At block 3 the dose rows rise steeply, the listed ones later: at every $\alpha$ from 0.5 to 0.9 the \fmtListA{} flip lies below the \fmtNone{} one (a post hoc description). Half doses move only \NqHalfNoneMin{}--\NqHalfNoneMax{} of the free-form answers, so B1 and B2 fail; B-F1 is not triggered, nor is B-F2: at half dose the value read without a mention keeps a share of its natural identity effect larger by \NqBFtwoMin{}--\NqBFtwoMax{} than the key read with the list after. Following the pre-written reading, we describe this convexity without a threshold claim; the channel-ratio law of part C stays failed (\cref{app:lawresults}).

\subsection{What did not hold}\label{app:s9-misses}

Every line below counts as not supported (F2: triggered), whatever the margin; the decisive cells are those of \cref{tab:stage9}.
\begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{1pt}
  \item \textbf{Three near-threshold cells.} P5a at Qwen: E1's \fmtListA{} flip at block 11 differs from the natural patch's by $\NqEoneGapQwenSeven$ [$\NqEoneGapQwenSevenLo$, $\NqEoneGapQwenSevenHi$], against a margin of 0.1 (Mistral and Llama at the point, through \fmtListA{} at block 7: $\NqEoneDiffAfterSevenMistralSeven$ and $\NqEoneDiffAfterSevenLlamaEight$). P5b at Mistral: E4b's $\tau$ at block 3 is \NqTauEfourbThreeMistralSeven{} [\NqTauEfourbThreeMistralSevenLo{}, \NqTauEfourbThreeMistralSevenHi{}], against at most 0.7 (Qwen's \NqTauEfourbThreeQwenSeven{}, at the point). P3s at Mistral: the early \fmtListA{} flip at $l_b$ is \NqPthreeEarlyAfterMistralSeven{} [\NqPthreeEarlyAfterMistralSevenLo{}, \NqPthreeEarlyAfterMistralSevenHi{}], against at least 0.7 (\fmtLetter{}: \NqPthreeEarlyLetterMistralSeven{}, at the point). Each interval contains its threshold, so the data do not separate these misses from passes; the verdicts stand.
  \item \textbf{P1, through passages.} At Llama, OPTB's late flip at $0.45\,L$ (block \NqPsgOnsetFortyfiveLlamaEight) is \NqPsgLateOptbFortyfiveLlamaEight{} [\NqPsgLateOptbFortyfiveLlamaEightLo{}, \NqPsgLateOptbFortyfiveLlamaEightHi{}], against at least 0.8 (Mistral's \NqPsgLateOptbFortyfiveMistralSeven{}, at the point). The story part P1s holds at the point (Llama's \fmtBefore{} at block 16: \NqPoneMinLlamaEight{}).
  \item \textbf{POST, at Mistral.} A neutral sentence naming the candidates after the story partly closes the late window: from $l_b$ to $0.5\,L$ the late flip is \NqPostLateFromLbMinMistralSeven{}--\NqPostLateFromLbMaxMistralSeven{}, below 0.8 at blocks 10 to 16 (block 12: \NqPostLateTwelveMistralSeven{} [\NqPostLateTwelveMistralSevenLo{}, \NqPostLateTwelveMistralSevenHi{}]). Llama holds at the point (\NqPostLateFromLbMinLlamaEight{} at block 16), Qwen fully.
  \item \textbf{P3, also through passages at Qwen.} OPTA's early flip at $0.3\,L$ is \NqPsgEarlyOptaThirtyQwenSeven{}, against at least 0.5, because the options do not close the late window there (P2p's Qwen cell, \NqPsgLateOptaThirtyQwenSeven{}, fails; P2p holds through two of three models).
  \item \textbf{F2, on passages at Qwen.} OPTB $-$ OPTA at $0.3\,L$ is \NqPsgGapQwenSeven{} [\NqPsgGapQwenSevenLo{}, \NqPsgGapQwenSevenHi{}], below 0.1: hence the warning-only reading of the passages.
  \item \textbf{B1 and B2, by a wide margin.} Half-dose edits move \NqHalfNoneMin{}--\NqHalfNoneMax{} of the free-form answers, against at least 0.9 in every model; the listed parts hold (\NqHalfAfterMin{}--\NqHalfAfterMax{}).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{What is post hoc}\label{app:s9-posthoc}

Fixed before the run, in the frozen note and specification: the predictions, thresholds and falsifiers, the $l_b$ rule, the populations, rows and answer rules, the statistics and the readings; every verdict in \cref{tab:stage9} is the frozen scorer's. Post hoc: the pattern under test, found in stages 1--8; the wording that describes the window, which no pre-written reading covers; the ranges over models and the decisive cells of \cref{tab:stage9}, which select printed cells, and $l_b/L$ and the cell counts, arithmetic on printed values; the grouping of the misses above; and every comparison the note does not name (the dose comparison between formats, E4b's key share against its transfer, CAA's free-form and \fmtLetter{} flips, the rule's base rate). Reported without a prediction, as the note requires: the single-channel rows, the inconsistency and the cells outside the predicted ones. Not used: the sensitivity analyses, the held-out passages R and LETA, which the scorer prints and which decide nothing; no claim rests on them.
